examples.trans: Someone whispered Zyuzya to him, and Vitya answered just like that!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Эта смешная история пошла ещё со школы.
examples.trans: This funny story started back in school.

examples.text: Я не хочу делать ей ещё больнее.
examples.trans: I do not want to make her hurt even more.

examples.text: Представляешь, за меня ещё никогда никто не дрался!
examples.trans: Can you imagine, nobody has ever fought over me before!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: With my boyfriend, or rather he is gone now.

meanings.en: to go out, to come out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'walked out, left', paired with 'выйти'.

examples.text: Ну что, он ещё не выходил из офиса?
examples.trans: Well what, has he not come out of the office yet?

examples.text: Я выхожу через минуту.
examples.trans: I'm going out in a minute.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from/out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И ты знаешь, из неё слова не вытянешь.
examples.trans: And you know, you cannot get a word out of her.

examples.text: Зато я в школе на олимпиады по физике ездил!
examples.trans: At least in school I went to physics olympiads!

examples.text: Виктор Петрович, нам сейчас свежий изюм привезли.
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich, they just delivered fresh raisins to us.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'from the office' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Здесь лежит пропуск на работу, офис тут недалеко.
examples.trans: Here is an ID pass for work, the office is nearby.

examples.text: Ну что, он ещё не выходил из офиса?
examples.trans: Well what, has he not come out of the office yet?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, я сейчас.
examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.

examples.text: Подождите минуту.
examples.trans: Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Look what I've got.

examples.text: Я смотрю телевизор.
examples.trans: I'm watching TV.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сеня, вчера вечеринка у тебя получилась отличная.
examples.trans: Senya, your party yesterday turned out great.

examples.text: Денис, расскажи, как у тебя со Светой?
examples.trans: Denis, tell me, how are things with you and Sveta?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, it (is)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никак, это было просто чтобы Катя поревновала.
examples.trans: Nothing at all, that was just to make Katya jealous.

examples.text: Но я думаю, это даже к лучшему.
examples.trans: But I think that is even for the best.

examples.text: Мне об этом мой надёжный человек сообщил.
examples.trans: My reliable contact informed me about this.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лучайно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Wait, look, is that not him walking over there by chance?

examples.text: И случайно потерял этот конверт по дороге в такси.
examples.trans: And I accidentally lost that envelope on the way in a taxi.

examples.text: А вы случайно не Самсон?
examples.trans: Are you by any chance Samson?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is coming', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Ладно, мне пора идти и работать с продуктами.
examples.trans: Alright, it is time for me to go and work with the groceries.

examples.text: Поэтому извините меня, пожалуйста, мне надо идти работать.
examples.trans: So excuse me, please, I have to go work.

examples.text: Я домой идти боюсь, вдруг он караулить будет.
examples.trans: I am afraid to go home, what if he waits in ambush.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hey', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hey, listen, your name is Denis, right?

examples.trans: Hey, stop right there, we want to talk!

examples.text: Эй, ты что?

examples.trans: Tell me straight, was that a real threat just now?

examples.trans: I told him about our kiss, and we broke up.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'place' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Everyone go to your stations quickly!

examples.text: Было бы неправильно надолго отлучаться с рабочего места.
examples.trans: It would be wrong to step away from my workplace for long.

examples.text: И на вашем месте я бы промолчал о разговоре.
examples.trans: And in your place I would keep quiet about our conversation.

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Hey, stop right there, we want to talk!

examples.text: Вы серьёзно прибежали сюда просто со мной поговорить?
examples.trans: Did you seriously run over here just to talk with me?

examples.text: Поговори с ним.
examples.trans: Talk to him.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.text: Нет, я очень хотела бы увидеть его лицо!
examples.trans: No, I would really love to see his face!

examples.trans: I took it when I wanted to save Andrey from your idea.

examples.text: Я хочу кофе.
examples.trans: I want coffee.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'hold, take'.

examples.trans: Here you go, this is for you.

examples.text: Держи его!
examples.trans: Grab him!

examples.text: Ладно, держи. Вот, смотри.
examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

examples.trans: Vitya, in America everything works great for me.

meanings.en: to calm down, to settle down
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спокоиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'calm down', paired with 'успокаиваться'.

examples.text: Ну что, успокоился?
examples.trans: Well, have you calmed down?

examples.text: Успокойся, пожалуйста!
examples.trans: Calm down, please!

examples.text: Успокойся, всё хорошо.
examples.trans: Calm down, everything's fine.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.trans: Viktor, attention, Dyagilev is on his way to us right now.

examples.trans: Listen, does Sveta know that there is nothing between you two?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'speak', paired with 'сказать'.

examples.text: Привет, Света, с кем ты сейчас говорила?
examples.trans: Hi, Sveta, who were you talking to just now?

examples.text: Мы с тобой говорили о моём Никите.
examples.trans: You and I were talking about my Nikita.

examples.text: И правильно, пусть думает, что тебе тяжело говорить!
examples.trans: And rightly so, let her think that it is hard for you to talk about it!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Просто она ведёт себя так, будто мы встречаемся.
examples.trans: She just acts as if we are dating.

examples.text: Ей сейчас тяжело, ведь она с парнем рассталась.
examples.trans: It is hard for her right now, because she broke up with her boyfriend.

examples.text: Она в своём деле просто большой профессионал.
examples.trans: In her field she is simply a great professional.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я говорю серьёзно, мы с ней просто друзья.
examples.trans: I am speaking seriously, she and I are just friends.

examples.text: Я домой идти боюсь, вдруг он караулить будет.
examples.trans: I am afraid to go home, what if he waits in ambush.

examples.text: Ладно, я пойду, вдруг ещё один брат появится.
examples.trans: Alright, I will go, what if another brother shows up.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'личный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('great').

examples.text: Сеня, вчера вечеринка у тебя получилась отличная.
examples.trans: Senya, your party yesterday turned out great.

examples.text: Не только, у меня есть отличная идея.
examples.trans: Not only that, I have an excellent idea.

examples.text: Витя, в Америке у меня всё отлично работает.
examples.trans: Vitya, in America everything works great for me.

examples.text: Со своим парнем, точнее его уже нет.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'be'.

examples.trans: Maybe it is simpler to explain everything to her in detail?

examples.text: У меня есть машинка.

examples.text: Детство было трудное.

examples.text: Мы живём вместе.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'after all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Это хорошо, ведь мне он ничего не рассказывает.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вчера я пришла домой и не смогла врать.
examples.trans: Yesterday I came home and could not lie to him.

examples.text: Мне об этом мой надёжный человек сообщил.
examples.trans: My reliable contact informed me about this.

examples.text: У меня живот заболел, и я домой пошла.
examples.trans: My stomach hurt, and I went home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Денис, расскажи, как у тебя со Светой?
examples.trans: Denis, tell me, how are things with you and Sveta?

examples.text: Никак, это было просто чтобы Катя поревновала.
examples.trans: Nothing at all, that was just to make Katya jealous.

examples.text: Видел я вчера, как у вас после текилы было.
examples.trans: I saw yesterday how it was with you two after tequila.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Доброе утро, твой человек надёжный, но очень медленный.
examples.trans: Good morning, your contact is reliable, but very slow.

examples.text: Валя, скажи мне, что ты там творишь?
examples.trans: Valya, tell me, what are you doing over there?

examples.text: Ведь это отличное и взаимовыгодное сотрудничество для нас.
examples.trans: After all, this is excellent and mutually beneficial cooperation for us.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'why', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Зачем же ты тогда меня утром во дворе ударил?
examples.trans: Then why did you hit me in the courtyard this morning?

examples.text: Зачем ты пришёл?
examples.trans: What have you come for?

examples.text: Зачем это?
examples.trans: What's that for?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you (informal)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет, Света, с кем ты сейчас говорила?
examples.trans: Hi, Sveta, who were you talking to just now?

examples.text: И ты знаешь, из неё слова не вытянешь.
examples.trans: And you know, you cannot get a word out of her.

examples.text: А чего ты тут так громко кричишь?
examples.trans: Why are you shouting so loudly in here?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'then', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Тогда ты бы об этом сейчас не спрашивал.
examples.trans: Then you would not be asking about this right now.

examples.text: Где же мы теперь этого водителя найдём?
examples.trans: Where will we find that driver now?

examples.text: И тогда я сразу с тобой полностью рассчитаюсь.
examples.trans: And then I will immediately settle up with you in full.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'in the morning' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Доброе утро, твой человек надёжный, но очень медленный.
examples.trans: Good morning, your contact is reliable, but very slow.

examples.text: Пойдём скорее отсюда внутрь отеля.
examples.trans: Let us go inside the hotel from here quickly.

examples.text: Странно, но внутри денег ни рубля не было.
examples.trans: Strange, but inside there was not a single ruble of money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Там сейчас свежее мясо должны привезти, проконтролируй.

examples.trans: Listen, that guy lost his wallet in the courtyard.

meanings.en: to hit, to strike, to punch
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'дарить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'hit, struck', paired with 'ударять'.

examples.text: Зачем же ты тогда меня утром во дворе ударил?
examples.trans: Then why did you hit me in the courtyard this morning?

examples.text: Ну, давай, ударь меня!
examples.trans: Well, come on, hit me!

examples.text: Он ударил кулаком по столу.
examples.trans: He struck the table with his fist.
